text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Visiting U.S Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin has pledged to promote economic cooperation between Vietnam and America.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet told visiting U.S Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin that Vietnam is not to blame for the slow pace of progress in bilateral relations.
-- Vietnam expects to spend more than $4.7 million this year on programmes aimed at preventing AIDS.
-- Trade Minister Le Van Triet says Vietnam will continue to suffer a trade deficit for several years.
-- Justice Minister Nguyen Dinh Loc has told the National Assembly the amended Penal Code should specify tougher penalties for rapists, corrupt officials and drug offenders.
-- Interior Minister Le Minh Huong began a visit to China last week to strengthen relations between internal security forces from the two countries.
-- National Assembly deputies have called for stronger efforts in administrative reform.
-- Meetings were held on Monday to celebrate the 90th birthday of the former Communist Party Secretary General Le Duan.
-- Finance Minister Nguyen Sinh Hung and U.S Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin have signed an accord to reschedule Vietnam's wartime debts.
-- National Assembly deputies from Ho Chi Minh City have asked to be given more information about the state budget and banking operations.
